title: DET-26-02 SSH failed-authentication burst — search result row
event_type: Splunk SPL query result table, DET-26-02 (index=linux_auth sourcetype=sshd, stats-by-src_ip output)

callouts.explanation: The single source address the stats command grouped on; every other column in this row describes only this host's behavior, which is what lets an analyst treat the row as one candidate brute-force source.

47 failed lines against only 9 distinct connections shows OpenSSH's per-connection retry batching (MaxAuthTries) in action — this is the field DET-26-02 added specifically because distinct_connections alone would undercount the real attempt volume.

Only two account names (admin, root) targeted despite dozens of attempts is the credential-guessing signature the rule's threat hypothesis names explicitly, distinguishing this from a broad username-enumeration sweep.

213 seconds falls under the rule's 300-second cap, which is the explicit burst-speed bound DET-26-02 adds on top of DET-03-01 — this is the field that turns 'many failures' into 'many failures, fast.'

note: Illustrative/conceptual mock-up of a Splunk search-results row for teaching purposes; not a captured screenshot of a real Splunk deployment or its interface.
